title: partial-tarball-gcs-stream-debug-scratchpad
body:
Context:
- Trying to reproduce intermittent failures when loading v3.1 weights for 'redwood-opt-13b' from GCS. Failures show up as: EOFError / unexpected end of file / truncated tar errors in the serving process when shards are streamed rather than pre-fetched.
- Customer reported ~0.1% of requests hit this path; we only see it in high-concurrency Dedicated pool tests.
- Hypothesis: upstream upload produced a partial composite object or client-side streaming/resume interactions (range requests) cause truncated reads. Could also be a subtle race in streaming+torch.load mapping of storages.

Environment:
- Ubuntu 22.04, Python 3.10.13, torch 2.2.0+cu121, fsspec 2024.2.0, gcsfs 2024.1.0, serving runtime branch: feature/streaming-prefetch (local checkout).
- GCS bucket: gs://redwood-weights-prod (multi-regional), object path: models/redwood-opt-13b/v3.1/weights.tar.gz{.part?} 

Repro steps I ran (local mimic of runtime stream):
1) Basic download (works locally)
   gsutil cp gs://redwood-weights-prod/models/redwood-opt-13b/v3.1/weights.tar.gz ./weights.tar.gz
   sha256sum weights.tar.gz -> 0f8b3aab... (matches upstream manifest)

2) Simulate streamed chunked download with curl and partial closes:
   curl -f --fail --compressed -v --range 0-10485759 \n     -H "Accept-Encoding: identity" \ 
     -o chunk0.gz \n     "https://storage.googleapis.com/redwood-weights-prod/models/redwood-opt-13b/v3.1/weights.tar.gz"
   (repeat with ranges, then cat them together).
   -> When I introduce an artificial interruption (kill curl mid-transfer) and then concatenate, the tar is corrupted -> tar: Unexpected EOF

3) Using fsspec/gcsfs streaming open() + torch.load in a small script:
   from fsspec import open as fsopen
   import torch
   with fsopen('gs://redwood-weights-prod/models/redwood-opt-13b/v3.1/state_dict.pt', 'rb') as f:
       data = torch.load(f, map_location='cpu')
   -> Sometimes raises: EOFError: Ran out of input
   Stack excerpt: (truncated)
     File "/usr/local/lib/python3.10/site-packages/torch/serialization.py", line 713, in load
       magic_number = pickle.load(f)
   -> Means file object closed early / incomplete bytes read

4) Runtime-specific reproduction (container):
   - Startup logs show: "shard-3: failed to read expected bytes (got 1048572, expected 5242880)" then process attempts fallback to CPU but fails later with KeyError for missing buffers.

Observed error snippets:
- "tar: Unexpected EOF in archive"
- "EOFError: Ran out of input"
- "BadZipFile: File is not a zip file" (from an internal extractor that tries both tar and zip heuristics)
- "Checksum mismatch: computed=17d3... expected=4f2c..." (from my local verify step)
- Runtime log: "blob read returned 0 bytes for shard=5 offset=0 len=0" (we shouldn't be seeing zero-length returns on 200 responses)

Commands & outputs I used to double-check server-side object integrity:
- gsutil hash -m gs://redwood-weights-prod/models/redwood-opt-13b/v3.1/weights.tar.gz
  -> MD5: abcdef..., CRC32C: 1a2b3c
- gsutil ls -L -b gs://redwood-weights-prod | grep -A3 weights.tar.gz
  -> Size: 1976824320 (matches manifest)
- gsutil cp then local sha256 match -> matches in my runs

What fails in production but not locally:
- Our runtime uses ranged HTTP GETs and streams into an in-memory buffer, then hands file-like object to torch.load which expects file-like to be seekable (or at least not prematurely closed). In production we use an HTTP client with connection re-use and a proxy layer. Logs show occasional 200 OK with fewer bytes than Content-Length (we log expected vs received).
- The failure rate increases under high concurrency and after a recent nginx upgrade on the edge (possible keepalive / chunked encoding regression).

Hypotheses (ranked):
1) Partial object uploaded as composite (parallel upload) produced warped chunks that only surface when clients use range requests in certain alignments. (low-medium)
2) Proxy/nginx is terminating keepalive early or mis-handling Range headers when under load, leading to truncated responses (high)
3) Bug in gcsfs/fsspec streaming wrapper where .read() returns less than requested and we don't retry until EOF, causing torch.load to see truncated pickle stream (medium-high)
4) Runtime code incorrectly assuming file-like is seekable; when torch.load tries to use buffering it triggers unexpected behavior on non-seekable wrapper (medium)
5) Zombie upload with zero-byte tail (rare)

Fixes/troubleshooting attempted:
- Re-uploaded weights as a single-object (no composite) from CI runner with `gsutil -o 'GSUtil:resumable_threshold=0' cp weights.tar.gz gs://...` -> still saw occasional downstream truncated reads in prod (so probably not upload-only).
- Switched runtime HTTP client to underlying google-cloud-storage client (instead of custom okhttp) for a pilot; saw a drop in incidents but not zero.
- Added read-retry wrapper around fs.read() that loops until requested length or EOF; this made torch.load failures drop to near-zero locally. Need to evaluate perf/cpu cost.
- Instrumented runtime to log Content-Length vs bytes_read per request and the response headers; correlation: most truncated reads have Transfer-Encoding: chunked and no Content-Length header.
- Tried disabling nginx keepalive on edge proxies for a test pool -> incidents reduced significantly during the 24h window (promising).

Immediate next steps (todo):
- [ ] Roll back nginx keepalive change to a canary with 5% traffic and monitor for recurrence (Marcus to own).
- [ ] Add robust read-until-full helper in runtime (wrap fsspec file objs) and benchmark memory/cpu for large-shard reads (I will prototype).
- [ ] Add server-side verification step after upload (compute sha256 and store in metadata; serving runtime asserts blob checksum on first open).
- [ ] Check whether parallel composite uploads were used by the original upload pipeline (ask solutions-eng). If so, add a final compose+verify step.
- [ ] Create a small integration test that simulates chunked transfer close mid-stream (inject in the HTTP client layer) to prevent regressions.

Notes & odd findings:
- Found one object with matching gsutil hash but when streamed via proxy it returned early; suggests proxy-level truncation, not storage corruption.
- In a couple of reproductions, curl + --range + connection: close returned a shorter-body but status 200 (no 206 partial) which confused our client logic.
- When I wrapped the stream with io.BufferedReader and implemented a custom readinto that ensures full length, torch.load happy. That feels like a reliable mitigation but need to validate perf on 13B shards.

Reference snippets I dropped into a test script:
- robust reader wrapper (pseudo):
  class FullReadWrapper:
      def __init__(self, f): self.f = f
      def read(self, n=-1):
          if n < 0: return self.f.read()
          buf = bytearray()
          while len(buf) < n:
              chunk = self.f.read(n - len(buf))
              if not chunk:
                  break
              buf.extend(chunk)
          return bytes(buf)

- quick local verify flow:
  with fsopen(path, 'rb') as f:
      data = f.read()
      import hashlib
      print('sha256', hashlib.sha256(data).hexdigest())

Questions to follow up on:
- Do we have any global proxy/ingress change logs around 2026-02-24 to 2026-02-26? (suspected window)
- Can infra share tcpdump for a failed download in a canary pod? Need packet-level confirmation that connection closed early vs server sent all bytes.
- Should we add a checksum validation in the runtime open path (cheap safety that fails safe before handing to torch.load)?

Decision points:
- Short term: add full-read wrapper + as-canary nginx keepalive disable (low-risk).
- Mid term: fail-fast checksum verification + stronger telemetry around Transfer-Encoding and Content-Length for every object read.
- Long term: shift to prefetching shards to local disk for Dedicated pools where latency/bandwidth cost is acceptable.

Unresolved:
- Still seeing a small number of incidents (~0.03%) in the pilot even after the wrapper and nginx tweak. Need deeper network traces.

Timestamped log excerpt (prod pod x1) 2026-03-11 03:12:45 UTC:
- [03:12:45.122] shard=7 start read range=0-5242879
- [03:12:45.332] shard=7 headers: {Transfer-Encoding: chunked, X-Geo: us-central1}
- [03:12:45.842] shard=7 read bytes=12489 expected=5242880
- [03:12:45.842] shard=7 error: EOFError: Ran out of input

If anyone on call wants to pair on the tcpdump or nginx config, ping me (Priya). This scratchpad will be updated with results from the canary tomorrow.

-- Priya
